description: A sleek, contemporary East Asian-influenced residential perimeter fence or boundary wall photographed at dusk. The boundary wall is constructed from smooth rendered concrete or plaster in a warm grey-beige tone, with substantial square-section pillar piers capped with flat stone or concrete caps. Between the piers, a modern vertical-slat aluminium or painted metal railing in a medium silver-grey tone provides a semi-transparent boundary. In the background, the building facade is a floor-to-ceiling curtain wall of glass with slim dark aluminium framing, its interior glowing warmly amber through the glass. Cloud-free pale blue-grey dusk sky sits above the flat roof parapet. Two manicured cloud-pruned Japanese black pine trees in the far left background add an organic traditional Japanese garden element. Additional low boxwood or ornamental hedge plantings in the gate area trim the scene at ground level. The driveway or entrance courtyard surface is smooth pale grey concrete or stone paving. Three identical traditionally influenced East Asian post-cap lanterns are mounted atop the pier caps, receding in a one-point perspective down the length of the boundary wall. Each glows with warm amber light through frosted panels with a decorative lattice screen detail, casting a warm glow on the cap and the upper rendered pillar surface. Camera is at a standing eye-level, approximately 5–6 feet, shooting a three-quarter perspective down the length of the fence wall. Lens is a normal to moderate wide angle.
